newsitem.title: POLAND: Early zloty flat despite rate rise expectations.
newsitem.headline: Early zloty flat despite rate rise expectations.

text.p: The Polish zloty held flat against the basket in slow early Thursday trade but dealers said that the local unit could strengthen if official interest rates were increased as the central bank pledged.

The market already partly weighed an official interest rate rise, dealers said. But they said the zloty could strengthen further if a foreign capital inflow followed the rate rise, which the central bank said would be made within weeks.
"The zloty should stay pegged to minus one percent for now, but it could rise toward parity if official interest rates are increased," said Mariusz Wituszynski, dealer at Kredyt Bank SA.
At 0855 GMT the zloty was at -1.20/-1.25 percent from parity, against opening's -1.16/-1.25 percent and Wednesday's close at -1.14/-1.19 percent.
It was at 3.4615/25 to the dollar, against 3.4625/60 at opening and at 1.8885/00 to the mark versus 1.8860/75 in line with the U.S. unit's slip to the German mark on world markets.

Dealers said however that large foreign entry into Polish treasuries would probably only take place after uncertainty about next year's budget gap and the September parliamentary polls fade around the start of the fourth quarter of 1997.

On the money market one-day rates shot up to the 25-percent lombard rate on the first day of the new monthly reserve period after the central bank increased its drainage rates by about half a point to 23 percent over the last week, dealers said.
Overnight rates were at 24.33/24.99 percent against 24.30/24.80 percent at 0635 GMT. Tomorrow/next rates were at 24.37/24.99 percent against opening's 23.20/25.00.
The central bank had repeatedly said that if market rates approached lombard rate levels it would be forced to increase official rates, which have remained unchanged for over a year.
